native_result.query: In the PCA on the forms of capital analyzed in hundred-year time slices, during the Younger Bronze Age (1100-500 BCE), how does the principal component value of PC1 in the beginning of the period at 1100 BCE differ from the subsequent time horizons between 1000 to 500 BCE?
native_result.HypoA: The beginning of the Younger Bronze Age (1100 BCE) is associated with negative values on the first principal component (PC1), while the majority of time horizons (1000-500 BCE) are characterized by positive values on PC1. This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB: PC1 of the twelve forms of capital is an extreme outlier at the opening YBA horizon of 1100 BCE (+2.36 score units) relative to the 1000-500 BCE horizons (mean +0.75, range +0.41 to +1.14; contrast +1.61 units, ~+5.3 z-units vs the later-six spread); the later horizons form a monotonic declining continuum. The 1100 peak reflects both a genuine surge in metal hoarding (ZHort -0.33 -> +3.38, the strongest new YBA signal) and inherited late-OBA block values (ZCU_AU, Zhausgr, ZMonument carry over from 1200 BCE and account for roughly three-quarters of the gross positive contributions), after which the capital system relaxes and slowly declines through 500 BCE.
native_result.WorkflowB: capital.csv (39 hundred-year slices, 12 complete Z-columns) standardized; PCA on the full series via numpy eigendecomposition of the correlation matrix (sklearn unavailable); PC1 sign fixed by positive loadings sum; PC1 scores extracted for the 7 YBA horizons (1100-500 BCE); contrasts vs each later horizon and vs the later-six mean computed; per-variable contributions mapped to symbolic/social/cultural/economic forms; sensitivity PCA on YBA-only rows (constant ZKeform, ZSichel dropped) confirming the contrast (corr 0.992). Carry-over from 1200 BCE flagged: 7 of 12 variables repeat OBA block values at 1100; only ZHort is an independent new observation driving the peak. Descriptive contrast only (n=7).
